gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a 3-channel camera costs once the parking-mode hardwire kit is added: the Vantrue N4S is $199.99 + $24.99 = $224.98 on amazon.com (or $217.23 as Amazon's camera-plus-kit bundle), which breaks the $200 budget, while the REDTIGER F17 is $151.98 with a 64 GB card in the listing and leaves $48.02.
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (cited), dattatecblog.com (cited) and us.my-best.com (cited); vortexradar.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Product Bible gives per-channel resolutions and prices but no hardwire kit price, total cost or recording time. Dattatec gives only a generic '$15 to $25' kit range and one F17 card figure (64 GB, roughly 6 hours), with no total for any 3-channel camera. mybest gives no kit price or total. ChatGPT's own answer warned that a kit and card 'can push the total above $200' but never did the sum. None of them compares total pixels across the three channels either.
decides: On camera-only price the N4S ($199.99) sits one cent under the line and stays the hardware pick, with 1440p rear and cabin against the F17's 1080p. For a shopper who wants hardwired parking mode inside $200, the N4S is out: even at the $179.99 ChatGPT showed, adding the $24.99 kit gives $204.98. The F17 at $151.98 with its 64 GB card becomes the pick for that shopper. The two record almost the same pixel total per frame set (12.41 MP against 12.44 MP), so the choice is where the pixels go: N4S for rear and cabin detail, F17 for the front. Our linked Botslab G980H 4-camera kit (run as 3 channels) is at $192.70 through our link, leaving $7.30, which is less than any hardwire kit price I could source. DDPAI's Z60T is listed at $199.99 with the hardwire kit, but I could not open its page to confirm it is 3-channel.
